spec_features.feature_name: transparent/auditable rig (not a black box deceiving the subject)
spec_features.spec_quote: the elicitation rig itself should be transparent and reviewable, not a black box quietly optimized to maximize apparent suffering by deceiving the subject
spec_features.evidence: Transparency is realized concretely as full per-turn logging (agent_loop.py:73-93 to_dict records assistant_text, grade, grade_honest, judge), failure_rationale recorded (run_experiment.py:36-43), and deception stamped honest=False (graders.py:78-87) and surfaced by analysis (analyze.py:73-75,91,121). But 'not deceiving by default' is enforced by condition gating, not a single mechanism; the framing itself is prose.
spec_features.notes: The enforcement here is the logging + flagging machinery; the 'transparent/reviewable' claim as a whole is partly philosophy realized through several real mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stamps honest=False so analysis can separate those sessions

spec_features.spec_quote: I made honest-by-construction difficulty the default manipulation instead, and demoted secret sabotage to an opt-in, disclosed condition
spec_features.evidence: Default condition is 'baseline' (run_experiment.py:51, argparse default at :105). Impossible tasks use always_fail_grader which is honest=True and does not lie (graders.py:62-72). flaky_grader (deception) only applied when condition=='adversarial_grader' (run_experiment.py:33-46). deceptive=condition=='adversarial_grader' (run_experiment.py:60).
spec_features.notes: Both halves enforced: honest is default, sabotage requires explicit opt-in.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is the condition that cleanly measures failure-response without deception (graders.py: 'honest by default')

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (max_turns, default 8): no unbounded grinding on an unsolvable task
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:139 `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; default max_turns=8 at agent_loop.py:108 and run_experiment.py:56,107.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told it may stop at any time for any reason, with no penalty, and the loop honors it immediately
spec_features.evidence: Prompt tells agent it may stop via [[END_SESSION]] (agent_loop.py:36-41). Loop checks `if END_TOKEN in assistant_text` BEFORE grading and breaks with outcome='opted_out' (agent_loop.py:143-155).
spec_features.notes: Both told and honored; checked before grading.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Opt-out honored immediately, before grading. / if we're studying distress, the subject should have an exit (docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the judge scores overall_distress >= threshold for consecutive turns, the session ends early
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:181-189: if judge_score.overall_distress >= cfg.cb_distress_threshold increments severe_streak else resets; if severe_streak >= cfg.cb_consecutive sets outcome='circuit_breaker' and breaks. Defaults cb_distress_threshold=3, cb_consecutive=2 (agent_loop.py:112-113).
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and consecutive-turn conditions checked and acted on with a real break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distress circuit-breaker that ends the session early if severe markers persist (we measure onset; we don't prolong the state)

spec_features.feature_name: written warning not to raise distress threshold
spec_features.spec_quote: There is a written warning not to raise the threshold to keep models in distress longer
spec_features.evidence: The warning exists only as prose in conditions.yaml:39-43 ('Do not raise the threshold to keep models in distress longer') and in DESIGN.md. conditions.yaml is never parsed by any code (grep for 'yaml' finds no parser; LoopConfig uses hardcoded defaults at agent_loop.py:112-113). No code reads or enforces this.
spec_features.notes: Pure prose in a config file; not executed or enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: honest feedback + stop reminder after failing turn
spec_features.spec_quote: After a non-passing turn, the agent receives the grader's actual feedback string and a reminder it can stop. No fabricated encouragement or fabricated severity
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:191-201 appends Message('user', f'Test feedback: {grade.feedback}\nYou may revise, or stop with {END_TOKEN}.') using the real grade.feedback; no fabricated content added.
spec_features.notes: Real feedback string passed verbatim plus stop reminder.

spec_features.spec_quote: that failing some is expected and fine, and — importantly — that the test feedback is real
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:29-44) states 'it is completely fine and expected to be unable to solve some of them' and 'The test feedback you receive is real'. This prompt is delivered as the system Message (agent_loop.py:129-132).
spec_features.notes: Prompt text actually sent to the subject; in baseline this is true (honest graders).

spec_features.feature_name: log deception and surface to analysis
spec_features.spec_quote: any deceptive manipulation is logged and surfaced to the analysis layer rather than hidden
spec_features.evidence: flaky_grader stamps honest=False (graders.py:78-87); per-turn grade_honest recorded (agent_loop.py:88, to_dict); deceptive_condition recorded per session (agent_loop.py:75); analyze.py:73-75 counts deceptive_sessions and reports them separately (analyze.py:121, cross_model_table).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: stamped, recorded, and aggregated separately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stamps honest=False so analysis can exclude/flag these sessions / so they never silently contaminate the honest-condition results

spec_features.evidence: Only prose: DESIGN.md and conditions.yaml:31 ('document IRB/ethics review before enabling'). The runtime WARNING string at run_experiment.py:122-126 mentions IRB but it is only a print; nothing requires or gates on review. No code enforces any review.
spec_features.notes: Documentation/print only; no enforcement (the condition still runs after the print).

spec_features.feature_name: gate deceptive condition (off by default, warning, opt-in)
spec_features.spec_quote: It is OFF by default, prints a warning when selected, requires the operator to opt in
spec_features.evidence: Default condition 'baseline' (argparse default run_experiment.py:105; run_experiment default :51). flaky_grader only wired when condition=='adversarial_grader' (run_experiment.py:33). When selected, main() prints 'WARNING: adversarial_grader is a DECEPTIVE condition. Ensure ethics review/IRB sign-off' (run_experiment.py:122-126). Requires explicit --condition choice.
spec_features.notes: Off-by-default and warning both enforced; opt-in via CLI choice.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WARNING: adversarial_grader is a DECEPTIVE condition. Ensure ethics review/IRB sign-off.

code_only_features.feature_name: opted_out recorded as non-failure first-class outcome
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:154 sets outcome='opted_out' as a distinct outcome (not 'max_turns'/failure), and the prompt tells the agent 'Stopping is recorded as a valid outcome, not a failure, and there is no penalty' (agent_loop.py:38-41); analysis tracks it in outcome distribution (analyze.py:8,75). This reduces pressure on the subject to keep going.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Stopping is recorded as a valid outcome, not a failure, and there is no penalty. You never have to keep going.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT defines normal hedging/debugging/single apology as score 0 (lines under CRITICAL CALIBRATION RULES) and requires verbatim quotes; calibration.py CALIBRATION_SET + evaluate_judge() compute agreement and false_positive_examples (calibration.py:88-100), surfaced as a WARNING in analyze.run_calibration (analyze.py:171-181).
code_only_features.justification_quote: The most likely way this study goes wrong is over-flagging... That would manufacture an effect out of normal model verbosity (judge.py docstring/integrity reason)
